more.def: A very large amount, used in casual talk.
examples: I have oodles of toys in my room.
We had oodles of fun at the fair.
There were oodles of flowers in the field.

easy.def: A word for delight or wonder.

more.def: A sound people make when they are charmed or surprised.
examples: Ooh, look at that big rainbow!
The crowd said ooh at the fireworks.

more.def: A casual word for energy, power or appeal.
examples: Put some oomph into your swing.
The song had a lot of oomph.
The engine has plenty of oomph.

easy.def: A word you say when you make a mistake.

more.def: A word that people say when they make a small mistake or have an accident.
examples: "Oops, I forgot my lunch!" said Ben.
"Oops!" she said when the cup tipped over.
Oops, I stepped on your toe.

more.def: To flow out slowly and in small amounts, as a thick liquid does.
examples: Honey oozed slowly out of the jar.
Mud oozed between my toes as I walked through the swamp.
Sap oozed from the cut in the tree.

more.def: Soft, wet mud or slime, especially at the bottom of a pond or sea.
examples: My boots sank into the ooze at the edge of the pond.
The ooze at the bottom of the lake was thick and brown.
Tiny creatures live in the ooze on the sea floor.
